author: Jim Breem
title: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s US Investment Plan; More Cash for the Shareholders!!!
text:
January 17, 2018 Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s US Investment Plan; More Cash for the Shareholders!!! 
Most of the time, Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) has come under major criticism, for building much of its popular products in China. But as iPhone maker said, it also will make $30 billion in capital expenditures in United States, over the time span of next 5 years, in part from opening data centers, to meet the growing demand, for services like iCloud is a good move. 
This move by Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) will create more than 20,000 new jobs, at the existing campuses of Apple and a new one. At the start Apple is not disclosing the location, just for technical support, at an unnamed location, and most probably setting off a scramble among the states and citie,s vying for bragging rights. 
“Apple is a success story that could only have happened in America, and we are proud to build on our long history of support for the U.S. economy,” said Tim Cook, Apple’s CEO. 
An analyst of Atlantic Equities James Cordwell said that Apple’s U.S. investment plan could make it easier for the company to give more cash to shareholders. 
“Being seen to just hand the cash back to shareholders could spark some political sensitivities,” and the spending announcement could be part of Apple’s efforts to manage this issue, Cordwell said. 
Trump described the move by Apple as a victory for his efforts. 
“I promised that my policies would allow companies like Apple to bring massive amounts of money back to the United States. Great to see Apple follow through as a result of TAX CUTS,” Trump wrote on Twitter. 
Asked in an interview with ABC News whether the job creation announcements were directly related to the Republican tax plan, Apple Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook gave a measured response. 
“Let me be clear: There are large parts of this that are a result of the tax reform, and there’s large parts of this we would have done in any situation,” Cook said in the interview. 
Apple is shouldering a big tax bill, as the iPhone maker brings back much of its estimated $252 billion cash held overseas, now it is quieting another long-standing complaint from lawmakers: that the world’s most valuable company avoids paying some U.S. taxes because it keeps so much of its profits outside the U.S. Apple said the $38 billion payment would likely be the largest of its kind. 
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) also said it would boost its advanced manufacturing fund, used to provide capital and support to suppliers such as Finisar Corp (FNSR) and Corning Inc (GLW) from $1 billion to $5 billion. For U.S.-based suppliers, Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) said it planned to spend $55 billion with in 2018, up from $50 billion last year.
